title: Pakistan Economy: Key Indicators Every Business Owner Should Watch in 2026
description: Inflation, policy rate, exchange rate, exports and tax policy: how Pakistan's economic indicators affect pricing, cash flow, financing and expansion plans for businesses.
lead: Inflation, policy rate, exchange rate, exports and tax policy: how Pakistan's economic indicators affect pricing, cash flow, financing and expansion plans for businesses.
body:
Every business in Pakistan operates inside the national economy. Knowing which indicators move your costs and revenues helps you plan better, even if you are not an economist. This article summarises what to watch. It is general information, not investment advice, and figures change often.

1. Inflation

Inflation affects the price of raw materials, salaries, rent and utilities. When it rises, margins shrink unless you revise prices. Track the monthly consumer price index published by the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics and review supplier contracts regularly.

2. The policy rate and borrowing costs

The State Bank of Pakistan sets the policy rate, which influences bank lending rates. Higher rates make working-capital finance more expensive and can delay expansion. Lower rates support investment but may change deposit returns. Build interest cost into your cash-flow forecast.

3. Exchange rate (PKR)

Importers feel currency movement immediately through landed cost; exporters benefit when the rupee weakens but face input-cost pressure. Consider pricing clauses, forward planning with your bank and keeping accurate foreign-currency records for tax.

4. Exports and remittances

Exports and remittances support foreign-exchange reserves. Sectors such as IT services, textiles and agriculture continue to be important, and special tax treatment often applies to exporters.

5. Tax and regulatory policy

The annual Finance Act can change income tax slabs, withholding rates and sales tax rules. Review the changes soon after each budget and update your pricing, payroll and compliance calendar.

Practical steps

  • Prepare a 12-month cash-flow forecast and update it quarterly
  • Keep clean books so lenders and investors can trust your numbers
  • Register with FBR and provincial authorities to avoid higher non-filer costs
  • Consider diversifying into export markets
